title: Migration Strategies
description: Plan and execute migrations from other version control systems to Git while preserving history, branches, and metadata.

data.text: Migrating to Git is rarely just a file copy. Teams migrate from SVN, Mercurial, Perforce, or TFVC because Git has become the industry standard. A careful migration preserves years of commit history, branch relationships, and author metadata while giving teams a clean working repository on day one.

Before running any conversion tools, audit the source repository. Identify the trunk or mainline branch, large binary assets that may belong in LFS, and any vendor branches or tags that must survive the transition.

items: **Map branches** — Identify which source branches map to `main`, `develop`, and long-lived support branches.
**Preserve tags** — Tags often mark releases. Losing them breaks downstream deployment scripts.
**Author mapping** — SVN stores authors as usernames; Git needs `Name <email>` pairs. Build a mapping file before import.

data.text: SVN to Git with git svn
`git svn` bridges Subversion and Git. It can clone an SVN repository into a local Git repo, fetch new revisions, and even dcommit back to SVN if you need a bidirectional bridge during transition.

data.title: Clone an SVN repository into Git
data.code:
# Clone the trunk and all tags/branches
git svn clone \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  https://svn.example.com/project \
  project-git

cd project-git

# Verify history

git log --oneline | head

data.text: For non-SVN systems, `git fast-import` reads a stream of Git objects from stdin. Many migration tools can emit this stream directly. On the Git side, `git fast-export` produces a portable stream, useful for splitting or rewriting history after import.

data.title: Rewrite author emails after import
data.code:
git filter-repo --mailmap authors.map

# Or with git fast-export / fast-import
git fast-export --all | \
  sed 's/old@example.com/new@example.com/g' | \
  git fast-import

data.title: Validate before you switch
data.text: After migration, compare commit counts, tag dates, and branch tips between the old and new repositories. Automate this validation so you can prove the migration succeeded before announcing it to the team.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Map branches, tags, and authors before starting any migration.
Use `git svn` for Subversion migrations and `git fast-import` for other systems.
Validate history completeness before handing over the new repository.
Rewrite author metadata early so email addresses are correct from day one.
